title: Same-named modules named by directory stay distinct modules in the Partials config
claim: Verdict: kept. `_module_key` joins a qualified macro's directory segments to the module with `File.join`, so `./drv` and `drv` give one module and `a/util` and `b/util` give two. Validation rejects an empty or quoted module, a module carrying a path, and a directory that is empty, quoted, absolute, or holds `..`. The experiment confirms two distinct generated Partials for the two modules.

title: Generated Partial filenames for _AT macros carry the macro's directory, which the docs table omits
claim: Verdict: partly kept. The overview table lists `ceedling_partial_<module>_impl.h` and the sibling patterns. For `_AT` macros the file is `<dir>/ceedling_partial_<module>_impl.h`: `form_partial_filename` puts the directory first and the prefix on the basename. The unqualified macros name a file with no directory.

title: Partials are generated into a partials build directory
claim: Verdict: kept. Generated Partial files sit below `<build root>/test/partials/<test path>/_t_/`, one root per test, mirrored by directory for `_AT` macros.

title: A plain Partial build links only the Partial, never the module's own object
claim: Verdict: kept. The linker command for the same-named experiment lists the test object, `a/` and `b/` `ceedling_partial_util_impl.o`, the runner and Unity. No object of `src/a/util.c` or `src/b/util.c` is linked.

title: The unqualified Partial macro with two same-basename modules picks the first by search-path priority
claim: Verdict: partly kept. The docs say the macros "expand into the unique names of the generated Partials header files". `TEST_PARTIAL_PUBLIC_MODULE(util)` with `src/a/util.c` and `src/b/util.c` names one Partial. Ceedling logs `Multiple files matched 'util.c' but chose 'src/a/util.c' by search-path priority` and the test passes against `a/`'s code. Only the `_AT` macros name two.

title: test:path matches a substring of the test's directory, not of its whole path
claim: Verdict: partly kept. The docs say "tests whose path contains the given string". The code tests `File.dirname(test).include?(arg)` on the project-relative test path, with `\` turned into `/`. With tests in `test/unit`, `test/unit_extra` and `test/integration`: `test:path[unit]` ran 2 tests (substring, so `unit_extra` too), `test:path[nit]` ran 2, `test:path[t/in]` ran 1, `test:path[unit/]` found none (no trailing separator in a dirname), `test:path[test_foo.c]` found none (filename excluded) and `test:path[Test]` found none (case).

title: test:pattern matches a regular expression against the project-relative test path
claim: Verdict: kept. The code applies `test =~ /#{regex}/` to each collected test path. Collected paths are relative to the project, so `^test/unit/` matched one test and the absolute directory of the project is never part of the text (`test:path[gap-10]` found nothing).

title: test:<name> takes as much trailing path as needed and names every match when ambiguous
claim: Verdict: kept. With `test/unit/test_foo.c`, `test/integration/test_foo.c` and `test/unit_extra/test_foo.c`, `test:test_foo.c` stops with `Ambiguous file reference 'test_foo.c' found. Include more trailing path` and lists all three. `test:unit/test_foo.c` and `test:unit\test_foo.c` each run one test. The lookup is `PathMatcher` in strict mode.

title: The bullseye: and gcov: tasks reuse the test: name, pattern and path rules
claim: Verdict: kept. Both plugins resolve a single-file task with `TestTaskName.test_name` and `find_test_file_from_name`, so trailing-path disambiguation matches `test:`. Their `path` tasks use the same `File.dirname(test).include?` test, so the `test:path` limits apply to them too. Read only. I did not run these plugins.

title: ceedling paths:header does not exist; the task is paths:include
claim: Verdict: broken. The reference lists `ceedling paths:header`. Ceedling defines a `paths:<name>` task for each key of `:paths`, and the standard sections are test, source, include and support. `ceedling paths:header` ends with `Unrecognized build task`. `paths:include` lists the include paths. The getting-started page repeats the error by listing `files:*` variants under `paths:*`.
